paragraphs.title: The Assembly Before the Lord and the Second Test

easy.explanation: The passage says that Satan also came among the sons of God before the LORD.
easy.q: Who came among the sons of God to present himself before the LORD?

answers: Job would remain faithful only while his body was unharmed
Job wanted to leave his land
easy.explanation: Satan claimed that Job would not remain faithful if his body were touched.
easy.q: What did Satan claim about Job's faithfulness?

easy.explanation: The LORD permitted Satan to attack Job but commanded him to save his life.
easy.q: What did the LORD command Satan to preserve?

answers: To test whether Job's faithfulness depended on his physical health
To make Job leave the land
medium.explanation: Satan argued that Job would give everything for his life and would curse God if his body were harmed.
medium.q: Why did Satan ask to touch Job's bone and flesh?

answers: Moving about from place to place
medium.explanation: Satan said he had been going to and fro and walking up and down in the earth.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does the phrase “going to and fro” mean?

answers: He could not touch Job's body
He could not speak to Job's friends
He could not take Job's life
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.”
medium.q: What limit did the LORD place on Satan's power over Job?

answers: The second test attacks Job's body, not merely what he possesses
The second test concerns Job's friends instead of Job
The second test concerns only Job's location
challenge.explanation: Satan's second accusation focused on Job's physical suffering rather than his possessions.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the first test and the second test?

answers: The second test was limited and did not include killing Job
Satan could attack only Job's possessions
challenge.explanation: The command shows that Satan's permission had a clear boundary: Job's life had to be preserved.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the command to “save his life”?

answers: That Job was the richest man alive
That Job was wiser than all his friends
That Job still held fast his integrity
challenge.explanation: The LORD says that Job still held fast his integrity despite his earlier suffering.
challenge.q: Which quality of Job does the LORD emphasize?

short_answers.question: What did Satan say a man would give for his life?
short_answers.explanation: Satan said, “all that a man hath will he give for his life.”

paragraphs.title: Job's Illness and His Wife's Response

easy.explanation: Satan smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
easy.q: With what did Satan smite Job?

easy.explanation: Job took a potsherd, or piece of broken pottery, to scrape himself.
easy.q: What did Job use to scrape himself?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that Job sat down among the ashes.
easy.q: Where did Job sit during his illness?

medium.explanation: Job's wife said, “Curse God, and die.”
medium.q: What did Job's wife tell him to do?

medium.explanation: A potsherd is a fragment of pottery, which Job used to scrape his sores.
medium.q: In this passage, what is a “potsherd”?

medium.explanation: Job told her that she spoke as one of the foolish women, rejecting her advice.
medium.q: How did Job respond to his wife's words?

answers: Nothing should be received from God
Both good and evil may be received from God
challenge.explanation: Job asked, “shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?”
challenge.q: What principle did Job express about good and evil?

answers: He continued to hold fast his integrity
challenge.explanation: Job did not sin with his lips, showing that he remained faithful.
challenge.q: What does Job's response show about his faithfulness after his body was afflicted?

answers: He did not sin with his lips
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes, “In all this did not Job sin with his lips.”
challenge.q: What final detail emphasizes Job's restraint?

short_answers.question: What did Job say they should receive from the hand of God?
short_answers.explanation: Job said, “shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?”

easy.explanation: The passage identifies Job's three friends.
easy.q: How many friends came to Job?

answers: To mourn with him and comfort him
easy.explanation: They made an appointment to come to mourn with Job and comfort him.

answers: They wept, tore their garments, and sprinkled dust on their heads
easy.explanation: Their actions expressed grief when they saw Job's condition.
easy.q: What did the friends do when they saw Job?

answers: Job was hiding in his house
medium.explanation: Job's suffering had altered his appearance so severely that they did not know him from afar.
medium.q: Why did Job's friends not recognize him from a distance?

medium.explanation: The friends came to express sorrow and share Job's suffering.
medium.q: What does “to mourn with him” mean?

answers: They wept, tore their garments, and sprinkled dust
medium.explanation: The passage gives this exact sequence of mourning actions.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the friends' actions?

answers: They did not know one another
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that they coordinated their journey to visit Job.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the friends coming every one from his own place and making an appointment together?

challenge.explanation: These were visible signs of grief and mourning.
challenge.q: What did tearing their garments and sprinkling dust express?

answers: They came to comfort Job but did not recognize him from afar
They came without hearing about his suffering
They came intending to harm him
challenge.explanation: They came with compassion, yet Job's condition was so severe that they could not recognize him at a distance.
challenge.q: What is striking about the friends' arrival?

short_answers.question: Name one of Job's friends mentioned in this passage.
short_answers.explanation: The passage names Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite.

easy.explanation: They sat with Job upon the ground seven days and seven nights.
easy.q: How long did Job's friends sit with him?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “none spake a word unto him.”
easy.q: Did the friends speak to Job during that time?

answers: That his grief was very great
That he was ready to travel
easy.explanation: They remained silent because they saw that Job's grief was very great.
easy.q: What did the friends see in Job?

answers: They saw that his grief was very great
They did not want to comfort him
medium.explanation: The verse directly connects their silence with the greatness of Job's grief.
medium.q: Why did Job's friends remain silent?

answers: No one said anything to him
They spoke to him from far away
medium.explanation: The statement means that the friends said nothing to Job during those days.
medium.q: What does “none spake a word unto him” mean?

answers: They left because his grief was great
They stayed silently because his grief was great
medium.explanation: Their continued presence and silence were a response to the depth of his suffering.
medium.q: What relationship exists between their silence and Job's grief?

challenge.explanation: Sitting beside Job for seven days showed that they were present with him in his grief.
challenge.q: What did the friends' presence express even though they did not speak?

answers: They moved from outward mourning to silent presence
challenge.explanation: They first wept and mourned visibly, then sat quietly beside Job.
challenge.q: What does the order of events show about the friends' response?

answers: Job's grief was too great for ordinary conversation
They did not want to be his friends
challenge.explanation: The verse explains that they saw his grief was very great, making silent companionship fitting.
challenge.q: Why was silence an appropriate response in this scene?
